difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for an integral regular scheme X of dimension at most 1, a coherent module F is torsion free if and only if it is finite locally free (source lines 1797-1806). One direction is immediate; for the converse the proof shows that a torsion free F has free stalks, which suffices by finiteness of the module and the local freeness criterion. The case dim O_{X,x} = 0 is a field, and in the case dim O_{X,x} = 1 the local ring is a discrete valuation ring, so torsion freeness of F_x makes it free over the DVR.
